reviews.title: Terrible
reviews.text:
This app is terrible, as someone said it had a solid streak for a few months where it was working well. 

As others have said if you pause a show mid-segment and then pause it, it restarts the entire segment. I’m now having issues where if I’m on a delay parts of the segment are blacked out. 

Trying to listen live is a coin flip. Sometimes it works, other time it freezes and just spins. If I didn’t pause throughout the day for calls I would just listen to WFAN on SiriusXM but you cannot listen on a delay since it’s only a broadcast deal.

reviews.title: Skip ahead, rewind, and restart
reviews.text:
I’ve been listening to 106.7 for years, almost exclusively the early morning show. I don’t know if this is something that’s part of a recent update or what but I am finding the app totally unusable. 

Over the years I’m used to the audio randomly cutting back 10-15 seconds once every 30minutes of listening time. Maybe I should hold a higher standard, but I used to it and it doesn’t bother me that much. 

But now…I’ve been trying to listen to this show from an hour in, and as soon as it hit the first commercial break it jumps to the live broadcast. Then when I try to rewind, it has to restart again. 

Beyond frustrating. Resigned to just tuning into the radio show elsewhere

reviews.title: So Sick of Audacy’s Nonsense
reviews.text:
I’m outting myself as a conservative up front so that all the “tolerant” left can stop reading and not be subjected to an opinion that’s different than their own.  
I can’t count the number of times I’ve tried to open one of the shows and/or podcasts I listen to only not be able to find it.  This includes podcasts that I’m
subscribed to. I can type in the exact name of the show or station and I still have to scroll through a seemingly endless list of stations or shows with similar — and sometimes, not so similar — names or call numbers.  Several times, podcasts were unavailable to me through your platform on the day of their release.  In the next day or two, I find out that there was indeed a podcast posted but it was unavailable to listeners.  Given the mostly glowing reviews I read of your app, I don’t think it’s a situation that most listeners experience.  The hosts of these podcasts often mention after the fact that for some unknown reason or glitch, a show wasn’t posted.  I’d like to think that it happens to shows and stations that are left-leaning but it’s too common an occurrence to believe that.

reviews.title: Feed Highjacking
reviews.text: Nearly every time I select play, Audacy highjacks my chosen station’s feed forcing me to listen to whatever commercials they’ve decided to shove down our throats, regardless of whether or not the station is live or not. I’ve confirmed this by immediately stopping play, then resuming play. The vast majority of times I do this, I find the station is actually live, meaning that Audacy regularly highjacks the feed of stations of content listeners have a RIGHT to hear. Upon addressing this issue with customer/technical support, they want my IP address to “assist” them in identifying the problem, which implies the “problem” lies only within the confines of my IP address. My issue with this is that I want this “problem” corrected/eliminated platform wide as I believe this “problem” is a tactic used by Audacy platform wide in order to nefariously increased their ad revenue on the box of consumers, free-radio-broadcast listeners!

reviews.title: After taking a break from Audacy, nothing has changed for the better.
reviews.text:
I took 3 months or so off from listening to WXRT in Chicago via the app. Nothing has changed I can see. The most frequent cutouts of any streaming app I use. Yesterday (Mon., 6/15), the Analisa mid-day show repeated the same 3-4 sentences in a row of her talking, then a commercial started to play on top of the repeats. 

If you’re not going to make this a usable app or fix your backend feed, then please just give the stream to Tune-In etc. 

I’ve also tried listening to this station via the iHeart Radio app, and while the cutouts are less, it seems to have the same glitches as the Audacy app. One would assume it’s Audacy’s back end that isn’t ready for prime time. It’s 2026 guys. Get with the program. 

WTTS out of Indy and 97.1 The Drive out of Chicago have their own apps, and they seem to work just fine.

reviews.title: Do not download
reviews.text: Probably the worst app I have on my phone. For every radio station to be promoting this, you would think the creators would have made a more reliable app. When connected to Bluetooth or CarPlay, the app won’t play unless it’s the last app you access on your phone. Meaning if you forget to have the Audacy app as the last page accessed, you will have to take your phone out and make the app your last screen in order for it to work. Even trying to change stations from the “recently listened”, if you sent a text message, you’ll have to go back in your phone and switch your last screen from “text message” to the Audacy app. It constantly cuts out for no reason at all, sayin there’s “no internet connection” even though your phone has service. Also, the repetitive ads are out of control. One morning, over two commercial breaks I heard 21 ads. Of those 21, 18 were for VRBO. If you’re gonna push the download of this app so hard, create a better product
